$comment: Non-secret settings for a PRODUCTION environment.
Copy to prod.json and fill in. Secrets belong in .env, never here --
the loader rejects any key containing key/secret/password/token/credential.
environment MUST match MIGRATION_HUB_ENV or the load fails naming both
values. prod.json declaring 'prod' while MIGRATION_HUB_ENV is unset is the
commonest first error: unset defaults to 'dev', which then looks for a
config/dev.json that is not there.
NOTE: only the key "$comment" is stripped before validation, and Settings
forbids unknown fields -- so put every note here. A "$comment_foo" key
makes the file fail to load.
THERE IS NO DEV TIER ON A CLIENT VM. Every command is a prod command and
prints so in yellow at startup, which means the banner is constant and easy
to stop seeing. dry_run and the concurrency limits below are the real
guardrails -- treat them as such.
Throughput values are deliberately conservative and must not be raised
until Moody's confirms their limits -- see
docs/api/open-questions-for-moodys.md item 6. max_concurrent_uploads is
per PROCESS, so three developers running one each is three concurrent
uploads against the same tenant.
stage_locally=false (the default) uploads straight from source_root, the
share RatCat wrote the backups to -- no second copy, no extra writes.
Set it true to copy into staging_root first: that path uses robocopy /Z, so
a network interruption resumes rather than restarting the transfer. Worth
it for a very large file over an unreliable link; pointless otherwise.
Leave staging_root pointing somewhere OTHER than source_root even when it
is unused -- if it is ever switched on, it writes batch subfolders into
whatever it names, and a later scan would rediscover those copies.
